high.title: Securities Companies' Views on VN-Index's Surprising Reversal
high.summary: The Vietnamese stock market continues trading near historical highs around 1,900 points on the VN-Index, but strong intraday volatility is increasing as money flows rapidly rotate between sectors. On May 20, widespread selling pressure caused the index to drop to 1,860 points before a strong recovery helped it close slightly positive. Dragon Capital Securities (VDSC) noted the market experienced a cautious correction session, with the index negating previous gains and closing at 1,912.93 points. The 50-point intraday swing showed unclear market support with red dominating. This volatility reflects intense market tug-of-war after rapid gains dependent on large-cap stocks. For FX and bond investors, this suggests potential capital rotation and risk-off sentiment that could impact VND stability and government bond demand as investors reassess risk appetite at these elevated levels.

high.title: Investors Wonder if They "Lost Out" After VN-Index's 50+ Point Reversal
high.summary: After the VN-Index "roller coaster" that saw it lose over 50 points before strongly recovering late in the session, many investors wonder if large money flows are returning to "accumulate" or if bull trap risks remain. Market expert Luong Duy Phuoc from Kafi Securities noted the volatility reflects intense market tug-of-war after rapid gains heavily dependent on large-cap stocks. When blue-chip stocks faced profit-taking pressure, selling quickly spread to other sectors, especially those that had run up strongly recently. However, the strong late-session recovery shows buying interest remains at lower levels, indicating the market hasn't fallen into uncontrolled selling and money is ready to deploy when stock prices offer attractive discounts. This suggests underlying liquidity remains supportive, which is positive for VND stability and could maintain foreign investor confidence in Vietnamese assets.

high.title: Banks Lend Trillions to Each Other: Vietcombank, VietinBank, BIDV and Agribank Are Major Creditors, VPBank and MB Net Borrowers of Large Liquidity
high.summary: Data as of end-March 2026 shows Vietcombank has 581.522 trillion VND in deposits and loans to other credit institutions versus 367.185 trillion VND in deposits and borrowings from others, creating a positive spread of 214.337 trillion VND - reflecting massive net lending in the interbank market. VietinBank ranks second with a positive spread of 138.361 trillion VND, while BIDV has 91.471 trillion VND. Combined, these three state banks create approximately 444 trillion VND in net lending, highlighting their central role in liquidity distribution. This concentration of interbank liquidity provision among state banks is crucial for monetary policy transmission and VND stability. Any stress in these institutions could significantly impact system-wide liquidity and potentially pressure the SBV to inject more liquidity, affecting money market rates and bond yields.

medium.title: Gold Ring and Gold Bar Prices Morning of May 21
medium.summary: International gold prices opened at $4,538/ounce, down 0.1% from the previous close, after gaining 1.4% on May 20. Gold rallied as expectations of easing Iran conflict reduced oil market pressure, cooling inflation concerns and pulling US Treasury yields from recent peaks. The 10-year Treasury yield decline after hitting January 2025 highs helped reduce opportunity costs for holding non-yielding gold assets. This gold price recovery amid lower US yields could influence Vietnamese gold market sentiment and potentially impact VND demand as a safe haven alternative.

medium.title: Gold Ring and Gold Bar Prices Evening of May 21: All Decline Compared to Morning
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices retreated in the afternoon after strong morning gains, with most brands declining 1.1-1.6 million VND/tael from morning levels. SJC gold bars traded at 159.4-162.4 million VND/tael, while gold rings traded at 158.9-161.9 million VND/tael. The volatility in gold prices reflects ongoing uncertainty about global monetary policy and could influence VND hedging demand, particularly as international gold price movements often correlate with emerging market currency flows.

medium.title: Real Estate Association Chairman: State Bank Reports Lending Rates Are Falling But Businesses Still Face Higher Borrowing Costs
medium.summary: HoREA Chairman Le Hoang Chau noted that while the SBV's Circular 08 modification allows 20% of Treasury deposits to count toward bank liquidity (improving state bank funding capacity), credit growth targets remain challenging. The SBV set 2026 economy-wide credit growth at around 15%, significantly lower than 2025's 19.1%. Real estate credit grew over 24% last year according to official SBV data. This disconnect between official policy rates and actual lending rates suggests persistent liquidity constraints that could keep money market rates elevated and support government bond yields.

medium.title: "Silent Disease" of Banking System Pushes Interest Rates Higher: Will State Bank's "Pressure Valve" Be Enough to Cool Down?
medium.summary: Money market dynamics show strong volatility in both retail (banks-public) and interbank markets, with deposit mobilization growth slowing at many banks. The SBV recently made technical adjustments to the loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR) amid concerns about increasing system liquidity dependence on Treasury flows and maturity mismatches between short-term funding and medium/long-term credit needs. Expert analysis suggests these structural issues may be core reasons for persistently high interest rate levels, with implications for VND funding costs and government bond market dynamics.
